# Adolescent health care

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Psychiatry > Childhood and neurodevelopmental disorders > Adolescent health care*

[Original Article Link](/library/GG0B03)

---

## Summary

<u>Adolescence</u> is a significant stage of development between childhood and adulthood. The definition of <u>adolescence</u> varies, beginning as early as 10 years of age and ending as late as 24 years of age. Although individuals in this age group are generally considered to be in peak physical health, it is a period of rapid physical, cognitive, social, and emotional growth, and peers begin to influence the individual's development to a greater degree. During <u>adolescent</u> visits, establishing rapport and assuring <u>confidentiality</u>, when appropriate, is essential for relationship building. Annual health reviews in <u>adolescents</u> should include screening related to physical health, <u>sexual health</u>, mental and emotional health, substance use, and safety. <u>Age-appropriate immunizations</u> should be offered, and clinicians should also provide counseling and education (e.g., on <u>puberty</u> and development, prevention of <u>sexually transmitted infections</u> and <u>unintended pregnancy</u>, and digital media use). One-on-one time with clinicians helps prepare <u>adolescents</u> to manage their own health care. Additionally, <u>adolescents</u> may begin to access health care independently, and it is crucial to be aware of local laws governing <u>confidentiality</u>.

---

## Adolescent well-visit

### Approach [[2]](/library/W71PkR0)[[3]](/library/qr1CRR0)[[4]](/library/Rq1ly30)




An annual well-visit is recommended for all <u>adolescents</u>.




* Explain the purpose of the visit.

* Describe its components (i.e., history and examination, screening, counseling, and education).

* If a parent or guardian is present, explain that the <u>adolescent</u> will have some one-on-one time with the clinician.

* Explain the extent and limits of <u>confidentiality</u>.  [[4]](/library/Rq1ly30)[[5]](/library/3t1SWi0)

* Obtain history, including:

* Past medical and <u>family history</u>

* A complete <u>review of systems</u>

* Detailed psychosocial assessment

* Use the <u>SSHADESS</u> or <u>HEEADSSS</u> screening tools.  [[4]](/library/Rq1ly30)

* Assess the <u>adolescent</u>'s emotional development  and the quality of their relationships. [[3]](/library/qr1CRR0)

* Perform a complete <u>physical examination</u>.

* Provide recommended screening and counseling related to: 

* General physical health

* <u>Sexual health</u>

* Mental health, substance use, and safety

* Provide referrals and/or appropriate follow-up based on findings.





> [!WARNING]
> Be aware of state laws regarding <u>parental consent for minors</u>. [[4]](/library/Rq1ly30)




> [!TIP]
> If a parent or guardian is present, observe their interactions with the <u>adolescent</u>, and always interview the <u>adolescent</u> privately, verbalizing the <u>confidentiality</u> policy. [[4]](/library/Rq1ly30)




### General principles of <u>adolescent</u> counseling [[3]](/library/qr1CRR0)[[4]](/library/Rq1ly30)[[6]](/library/Sx1yDQ0)




See also “<u>General concepts of patient counseling</u>.”




* Assess for health risk behavior and identify strengths.

* Avoid making assumptions about <u>sexual orientation</u> and <u>gender identity</u>.

* Use educational materials with visual aids and plain language.

* Use <u>motivational interviewing</u> techniques.

## Developmental changes in adolescence

* <u>Adolescence</u> is a period of physical, cognitive, and psychosocial development. [[7]](/library/0aWeQP0)

* Increased risk-taking behavior during <u>adolescence</u> can increase risk of <u>morbidity</u> and mortality, e.g., from: ;  [[7]](/library/0aWeQP0)

* <u>Sexually transmitted infections</u>, <u>unplanned pregnancy</u>

* <u>Eating disorders</u>, <u>depression</u>, <u>suicide</u>

* <u>Motor vehicle accidents</u>, homicide

| <u>Cognitive development</u> | <br><br>* Impulsivity<br><br>* Growing intellectual interests<br><br>* Concrete thinking<br><br><br> | <br><br>* Growing interest in the future (e.g., long-term goals)<br><br>* Enhanced moral reasoning<br><br>* Expanding capacity for abstract thinking and problem-solving<br><br><br> | <br><br>* Abstract thinking<br><br>* Moral reasoning<br><br>* Improved impulse control<br><br>* Long-term planning and goal-setting<br><br><br> |
| Psychological development | <br><br>* Preoccupation with self-esteem and body image<br><br>* Mood swings<br><br>* Struggles with rules and desire for independence<br><br><br> | <br><br>* Increased sense of competence<br><br>* Experimentation with risk behaviors (e.g., <u>cigarette smoking</u>, <u>recreational drug</u> use, sex)<br><br>* Growing independence and resilience<br><br><br> | <br>* Firmer sense of identity and independence<br><br> |
